claims.text: The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ ("Output value errors") exists in the Pulumi docs.

The Output value errors troubleshooting page covers the `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` placeholder text and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
In Pulumi, calling toString on an Output<T> yields the placeholder text `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` rather than the underlying value.

When a Pulumi output is treated as if it were a plain value, the placeholder text `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` can appear in log lines, generated files, or resource properties instead of the expected value.

A Pulumi troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value as if it were a plain value.
In Pulumi programs, stringifying an output value, branching on it (e.g., in a conditional), or reading it like a plain value produces errors (or incorrect behavior) that can be diagnosed.

Pulumi produces a "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" error when another update is already running on a stack, and a page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ explains how to resolve it.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors, and a page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/server-errors/ on handling them.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/post-step-errors/ on troubleshooting post-step event failures and engine bugs.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/connection-issues/ on fixing network connectivity and proxy problems.

The Pulumi CLI emits `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` errors when it cannot access a self-managed (DIY) state backend, and the section anchored at #error-reading-pulumimetayaml in /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/using-a-diy-backend/ explains how to resolve them.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ on handling scenarios when `pulumi destroy` fails.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/interrupted-updates/ on recovering from interrupted Pulumi deployments.
On Apple Silicon Macs, running x86_64 Pulumi binaries under Rosetta 2 can cause crashes or hangs, and a page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/architecture-mismatch/ explains how to fix this.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/troubleshooting/ on resolving continuous integration and deployment pipeline issues.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/editing-state-files/ describing safe techniques for modifying Pulumi state files.

A recently deleted Pulumi stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`, as described at /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/restoring-deleted-stacks/.
The Pulumi CLI supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags that limit operations to specific resources, which can be used when a stuck or misbehaving resource is blocking a wider update.
The page at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/ covers automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging for debugging and diagnostics.
Pulumi dev builds are pre-release builds that let users access bug fixes that have not yet shipped in a stable release, as described at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/using-dev-builds/.
Pulumi has a Community Slack at slack.pulumi.com that provides fast community support.
A guide for filing GitHub issues exists at /docs/support/filing-issues/ and explains how to report bugs in the right repository.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
The logging guide at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/ has an 'automatic-logging' section (anchor #automatic-logging) that documents `pulumi logs share`.
Pulumi offers paid support options reachable via the /contact/ page.
Pulumi can be reached for questions or feedback via community Slack (slack.pulumi.com), GitHub (github.com/pulumi), or a support page at /support/.
Visiting the troubleshooting index page with the URL hash #conflict redirects to /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/, per pulumi/pulumi issue 20846.
Visiting the troubleshooting index page with the URL hash #verbose-logging redirects to /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/#cli-verbose-logging, per pulumi/docs issue 16985.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the resource providing them has been created or updated.
Representing resource properties as Outputs is central to how Pulumi builds a dependency graph and runs `pulumi preview`.
The Pulumi docs have a page on Outputs at /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/#outputs.
Pulumi docs pages exist at /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/ ('Accessing single outputs with Apply') and /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/ ('Working with multiple outputs').

When an output value is concatenated, logged, or converted to a string directly instead of via `apply` or an equivalent helper, Pulumi does not raise an error by default but silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.

In TypeScript, converting a Pulumi Output to a string via a template literal yields a string containing the text `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on a Pulumi Output, or letting one flow into a JSON body, produces the string `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` rather than the value.
In Python, converting a Pulumi Output to a string (e.g. in an f-string) produces a string containing `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and does not raise an exception.
In Python, converting a Pulumi Output to a string also causes Pulumi to log a warning.
In Python, passing a Pulumi Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
In Python, `Output.json_dumps()` is the Pulumi-provided way to JSON-serialize an Output.
In Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error rather than a runtime failure.
In Go, output values are resolved with `ApplyT`.

In C#, converting a Pulumi Output to a string via string interpolation yields a string containing `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`, with no exception thrown.

Because the string-conversion mistake produces a string rather than throwing, the program runs, `pulumi up` succeeds, and the placeholder text only surfaces later in a log line, generated config file, or downstream resource property.
Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` makes the same code throw an exception at the point of the mistake instead of returning the placeholder text.
The `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING` environment variable is supported in the TypeScript, Python, and C# Pulumi SDKs (not Go).
In TypeScript, `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` are the string-composition helpers for outputs.
In Python, `Output.concat`, `Output.format`, and `Output.json_dumps` are the string-composition helpers for outputs.
In Go, `pulumi.Sprintf` and `pulumi.JSONMarshal` are the string-composition helpers for outputs.
In C#, `Output.Format` is the string-composition helper for outputs.

A value read inside an `apply` callback is only available inside that callback (or in another output derived from it); assigning it to an outer variable and using it outside the callback yields `undefined` because the callback has not yet run.
The `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the rest of the program's top-level code has finished running.
The `apply` callback runs when the engine resolves the dependency graph, not on the program's clock, so adding a delay does not fix reading the value outside the callback.
Passing an Output such as `bucket.bucketName` directly as the input to another resource (e.g. `aws.s3.BucketObject`'s `bucket` argument) works without `apply`, and Pulumi resolves the dependency.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values.
A resource's logical name is a position that cannot accept an output.
The page contains a section anchored at #using-an-output-as-a-resource-name-a-map-key-or-a-loop-bound.
In a dynamically typed language, an `if` on a Pulumi Output evaluates the output object itself rather than its eventual value, so the condition is generally always true.
In a statically typed language, branching on an `Output<bool>` is usually a compile error because an `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.

A value known when the program starts, such as a stack configuration setting read with `pulumi.Config`, an environment variable, or a hardcoded flag, is a plain value that can be branched on normally.
When a branch depends on a resource's output, the branch must move inside `apply`, so both outcomes are expressed as values (e.g. `vpc.vpcId.apply(id => ...)`) rather than as program structure.
Passing an output as a resource's logical name or using it as a loop bound or map key fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#, where these positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using an Output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using a Pulumi Output as a dictionary key does not raise an error; Python compares and hashes the output object itself, so the lookup silently keys on the wrong thing.

To make resource names or counts depend on data only known after a resource is created, one can restructure dependent resources into a later, separate stack that consumes the first stack's outputs through a `StackReference`.
A Pulumi docs section on StackReferences exists at /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences.
Trying to `await` an output or read its value synchronously either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or quietly returns placeholder text.
Pulumi has no supported way to block a program and synchronously pull a resolved value out of an output.
Pulumi deliberately does not support synchronous reading of outputs because the engine would need the value before it has finished determining the order in which to create resources.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
A `StackReference` from another Pulumi program consumes one stack's outputs as another stack's inputs.
The Pulumi Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (for example `res.Outputs` in Go).
A Pulumi docs page on the Automation API exists at /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
`pulumi stack output`, `StackReference`, and the Automation API outputs field all read a value that has already resolved rather than unwrapping an in-flight output from inside the same program.
